driverRegime.method: daily % change of each asset regressed on the daily change in the US 2-year and 10-year yields (basis points) and on the daily % change in WTI; a driver is dominant when |corr| >= 0.4

dataNotes: Run timing: this cycle ran the morning of Thursday 12 November 2026 after the GitHub Actions fetch job drafted contracts/*.2026-11-11.json from Wednesday 11 November's close (Veterans Day - US stocks traded, the cash Treasury market was closed). Every figure used is dated at or before 2026-11-11. The Wall Street Journal report that Nvidia's board is preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang, and Nvidia's -8.6% after-hours move, were reported on the evening of 11 November (StockTitan/CNBC timestamps 6:05pm-7:59pm ET) and are used; news-log entries dated 12 November (pre-market moves, other earnings) were NOT used.

Bonds, dollar and IWM sigma are not auto-fetched; the last obtainable implied-volatility values (TLT 30-day IV, EUR/USD 1-month ATM IV, RVX) were carried forward again with stale-source notes. The fetched ^VIX (17.49), ^GVZ (24.21) and ^VXN (26.74) sigma gauges are all dated 11 November.

News-log entries for 2026-11-11 (six, matching the Artifact database exactly; no hand-entered entries) were read. A web search restricted to 11 November session wraps added: breadth, sector returns, VIX, dollar/FX, gold/oil closes, credit ETFs, SPY flows, Fed-speaker remarks and FedWatch pricing (CappNotes 'Closing Look - Wednesday, November 11, 2026'), and the after-hours Nvidia report (StockTitan live blog of 11 November).

Vendor conflicts: the fetched futures closes understate the cash-index gains (ES=F +0.67% vs S&P 500 +1.31%; NQ=F +1.05% vs Nasdaq-100 +2.28%) - futures settle later than the cash close, and part of the gap may reflect after-hours trading; the fetched closes are used. Gold is -1.5% on fetched GC=F closes vs -0.74% to $4,000.50 per CappNotes; the fetched closes are used. One Substack recap put the S&P 500 at 7,626.55 (+1.40%); the better-corroborated 7,619.38 (+1.31%) is used.

Category 1-12 votes are neutral unless a dated source gives a clear read: Breadth (1D, equity assets) is bullish on 11 November's broad advance; Fed path is horizon-wide and hawkish (fully priced December hike, Logan's two more hikes); Earnings catalysts are bearish 1D for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 on the after-hours Nvidia CEO report; gold's Cross-asset 1D vote is bearish on the dollar's 0.67% rise. Rates are neutral because the cash Treasury market was closed. Trend structure follows the computed structure reads; Market structure carries its own mechanical direction.

newsLog.event: US futures rise as an AI/chip rebound outweighs Tuesday's hot-CPI Fed-hike fears: Nasdaq-100 futures about +1.9%, S&P 500 futures +0.8-0.9%, Dow futures about +0.1-0.3%, Russell 2000 futures +0.4%. US bond market is closed for Veterans Day; stocks trade normally.
newsLog.reaction: Tech-led bounce after Tuesday's CPI selloff; December Fed hike still priced, Bowman says 'still work to do' on inflation.
newsLog.tickers: SPY, S&P, QQQ, Nasdaq, IWM, Russell

newsLog.event: CoreWeave beat Q3 estimates and raised 2026 revenue guidance to $13.0-13.3B, saying it won't issue more parent-level unsecured debt through 2027; record $133B backlog. Shares +14-17% pre-market, sparking a chip rally: Nvidia +4.9% (rebounding from two days of losses on the CEO probe; Baird cut to Neutral), Micron +6.5%, AMD +6.4%, Intel +6.2%, Broadcom +4.2%.
newsLog.numbers: CRWV rev $3.66B vs $3.55B est; adj EPS -$0.95 vs -$1.16 est; FY rev $13.0-13.3B vs $12.86B est; backlog $133B (+138% y/y)
newsLog.reaction: Eases AI-infrastructure debt jitters; semis lead Nasdaq futures higher.
newsLog.tickers: CRWV, NVDA, MU, AMD, INTC, AVGO, QQQ, Nasdaq

newsLog.event: Oil rebounds from a two-month low: Brent back near $92 (settled $91.49 Tuesday after touching $89.16) and WTI +1.5% to about $87.3, after Iran said tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz and its security chief said no talks are under way and enriched material won't leave the country.
newsLog.numbers: Brent ~$91.7-$92.8 (+0.2% to +1.4%); WTI ~$87.33 (+1.5%); 10 ships attacked in Hormuz in Nov vs 37 in Oct
newsLog.reaction: Fading hopes of an imminent US-Iran deal put a bid back under crude; energy stocks lead Europe.

newsLog.event: Overseas risk-on with a firmer dollar: MSCI Asia Pacific about +1.6% on tech, European stocks higher with the DAX near record highs. USD/JPY rose above 159.00, its highest in over two months, reviving intervention talk; EUR/USD slipped to about 1.1130. Gold +0.3% to about $4,044.
newsLog.reaction: Dollar bid on fully priced December Fed hike; Treasuries not trading (holiday).
newsLog.tickers: DXY, USD, dollar, GLD, gold, SPY, S&P

newsLog.event: US stocks closed sharply higher on Veterans Day (bond market closed, equities traded): S&P 500 +1.31% to 7,619.38, Nasdaq Composite +1.60% to 25,466.19, Dow +0.49% to 52,486.49, Russell 2000 +0.88% to 2,846.26. Apple hit a fresh record above $355, market cap ~$5.16T (+31% YTD). Nvidia rebounded 2.9% to $173.73 (faded from a near-5% pre-market pop) even after Baird cut its price target to $200 and downgraded to Neutral on CEO-probe and China-chip-export-curb worries; AMD +7.3% to $552.90, Broadcom +4.0% to $345.22.
newsLog.reaction: CoreWeave's beat-and-raise extended the AI-trade rebound into the close, outweighing a Baird downgrade of Nvidia; broad gains across megacaps and chipmakers.
newsLog.tickers: SPY, QQQ, DIA, IWM, AAPL, NVDA, AMD, AVGO

newsLog.event: Marvell Technology (MRVL) agreed to acquire optical-components maker Lumentum (LITE) in an all-stock deal, offering 4.5 MRVL shares per LITE share. Lumentum shares rose about 12% on the news, recovering alongside the broader AI-infrastructure/chip rally.
newsLog.numbers: Exchange ratio: 4.5 MRVL shares per LITE share; LITE +12.3%
newsLog.reaction: Consolidation play in the AI/optical-networking supply chain adds to the day's chip-sector rally.
